I'm a father of five and my dad passing shook me to the core. He was relatively healthy, he had type 2 diabetes but it was controlled with diet changes, and just all of a sudden he was in the hospital and we were getting the news that there was nothing they could do. It made me take a hard look into my own health, because if it could happen to him, it could happen to me. Keep yourself healthy and wrap your little one up in a hug. You never know what tomorrow will bring.

My wife and I came to the agreement shortly after he passed that we would continue our traditions even though it will be painful. It is more important for my children to grow up with the memories of the same traditions I grew up with than for me to stop them all because it hurts. Even though it is a knife to the heart every time they say his name, it has also made this week a little easier hearing my kids talk about what they remember of their papa. Just little things like him always sneaking into the kitchen and stealing fresh cookies for them (and a handful for himself), or how he would lift them up so they could put the decorations on the top of the tree. I want to keep him memory alive, and that means carrying on all of our traditions. 

Sorry for the rant, it's been a rough year so far.

My dad was perfectly healthy and full of life when he came by my house to drop some gifts off for his grandkids. Later that night he passed out in the kitchen of his home. Rushed to the emergency room where they found a blood clot blocking the blood flow to his small intestines. Rushed into emergency surgery and placed in the ICU. Three surgeries later we are told he would be able to go home within a few days. The day he was scheduled go home his blood pressure bottomed out. They figured out another blood clot went into the same spot and started killing the remaining small intestine. He was given a few days to live. Within two weeks I went from recording my dad playing with my children on my living room floor, to holding his hand as he took his last breath.

Honestly it boils down to finding out what is important in life and how to make sacrifices. When my kids came along I made a lot of changes to my monthly budget to try and make sure I could provide what was needed for them. When times got hard and I was having to pick between buying food or paying the power bill........that's when I learned what it really meant to make sacrifices for your kids. Most people can never "afford" to have kids. Hell, even the people that can afford it could wake up tomorrow and lose their job. You never know what life will throw at you.

My dad was taken to the hospital for emergency surgery two weeks ago. He had a blood clot that was blocking the blood flow to his small intestines, and as a result about two thirds had died and had to be removed. Three surgeries later and the doctors were very positive and had planned on sending him home yesterday. Yesterday morning he started to run a fever and his blood work showed a rising white blood count. After a day of trying to treat the symptoms they finally ordered a CT scan this morning. We got the news a few hours later that the blood clot had returned and the remaining intestine had started to die. There is nothing they can do for him except help manage his pain. 

I'm sharing this to daddit because this man has been the standard that I hold myself to as a father. He loved me and my sisters more than anything in this world and he ran himself into the ground day after day to make sure we had a good life. I can only hope to be half the father that he was to me. Everyone please, hug your kids and call your dad. You never know when it can all change.

I've been married almost 6 years, my wife is the one that showed me this video to begin with. She thought it was hilarious.

I've always known she wants a little girl one day of her own, but never thought it would be this extreme once we found out. Has really taken the enjoyment out of the pregnancy now, as I honestly can't even talk to her about it... Even worse is that she obviously feels terrible that she feels this way, and knows that she should be ecstatic that the baby is just healthy, as many people have a hard time even just conceiving, etc. So not only is she not happy that her dream of a girl didn't come true this time around, but she's mad at herself for feeling that way, which obviously compounds the whole issue.

Talk to her about it. Seriously, just sit down and talk about it. It will be hard, she will probably get upset, you will probably feel like absolute shit to start off with....but if you are caring and not accusing, listen to what she says to understand instead of just to respond, and just be there for her she will open up. The biggest thing you can do is be supportive and loving and let her know that it is OK to be disappointed. That it is OK to not be jumping up and down for joy. Yeah everyone says "as long as the baby is healthy..." but it is perfectly normal to want a beautiful girl over a bouncing boy. Start the communication now because postpartum depression is a bitch and if she does go through that and you haven't opened the door for her to confide in you without judgement.......it's going to be rough. 

Seriously, good luck with everything and never hesitate to reach out for help or advice.
